newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat as supplies thin out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat as supplies thin out.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were pegged in late trade on Friday from flat to 1/8 firmer in spots, as supplies thinned out, helping the market buck the downward pull of lower Treasury bonds.
"I think our prices are about the same," a trader said, noting activity was quiet due to an industry golf outing in Westchester County, N.Y.
Another trader said that index bonds gained as the June municipal futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade firmed three ticks to close at 116-13/32.
"Futures are staying firm today, forcing all the contract bonds to trade up," another trader said.
Later, he added: "But municipals performed extremely well all the day (but) it was more on the run issues, stuff in the contract or that mirrored the contract."
New York City sold $66 million of bonds to individual investors during the first day of the presale period, falling short of the $100 million mark it set during a mid-April sale.
A city official, noting the presale period did not begin until about midday, said: "We're going to take full advantage of the fact that we still have a day-and-a-half to go."
He noted that starting the sale before the weekend gives individual investors more time to figure out what they wish to do.
The retail presale period ends Tuesday at 1300 EDT, and New York City plans to go to the market Wednesday with the $739 offering of general obligation bonds.
The city typically starts the presale period for individual investors on a Thursday, and its decision to start on a Friday drew a bit of criticism.
"It's a beautiful, sunny Friday, normally phones ring off the hook, and we only got one call back," a trader said.

The city's sale of general obligation bonds was tentatively priced at a top yield of six percent in 2016 during the retail order period. This is the biggest offering on next week's negotiated calender.
Total municipal bond sales for next week were expected to add up to $3 billion in 116 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
On the competitive side, 79 sales totaling $1 billion were on the schedule. A $285 million Nevada issue on Tuesday was the largest.
The supply calender, though bigger than this week's approximately $2.2 billion, is part of a mainly falling trend in supplies seen since early April.
Secondary supplies also have tapered, with the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List totaling $1.06 billion, a bit on the light side.

The market remains pre-occupied with the May 20 meeting by the policy making arm of the Federal Reserve. Proponents and opponents of higher interest rates squared off at a panel discussion on Friday in Washington, though most agreed that the central bank was not likely to tighten credit next week.
June Treasury bond futures shed 11 ticks to 109-31/32. The MOB spread stood at 206 ticks, suggesting to some players that despite the drop in supplies, municipal bonds were overbought.
Chicago, Illinois, Board of Education of 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.85 percent, NET, up two basis points.
And Delaware River Port Authority Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of 2026, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.70 percent, down two basis points.
